Goals are more likely to be achieved when they are clear, measurable, and bite-sized. The objective is for team members to get in the habit of breaking down objectives into a series of subtasks.

 

 

 

 First, read this article on [Setting Effective Goals]( https://www.inc.com/disneyinstitute/effective-team-goals.html).

 

 ### Break goals into clear tasks

 

 When your team begins to work towards a goal, the team leader should start by specifying the ultimate objective (e.g., increase sales 10%). As a group, list the measurable results that need to be met to achieve it. For each of these tasks be as specific as possible and ask yourself the following questions:

 

 

 

 * How will we measure success?

 

 * How long will it take?

 

 * Who should own it?

 

 * How will it contribute to the ultimate objective?

 

 * What process will be used?

 

 

 

 Use this list to identify whether your goal is attainable and realistic. Get team member feedback and modify the tasks as needed. Track the team's progress to learn where you may have miscalculated to improve in the future.
